newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says clamping down on foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says clamping down on foreigners.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly Gazprom is keen to stop what it calls "swindlers", foreigners who are buying Gazprom shares on the domestic share market, chairman Rem Vyakhirev said on Thursday.

"We have already been looking at this problem for three years. We have caught red-handed foreign swindlers who are buying up shares cheaply here and then transforming them into different kinds of securities," he told a news conference.
Gazprom strictly separates shares for domestic and foreign investors, and its charter sets aside nine percent of its capital for non-resident investors.
A small part of this has already been issued in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADSs), which trade at a large premium to domestic shares in the company.
Vyakhirev decribed schemes whereby overseas investors had sought to buy Gazprom shares on the domestic market to take advantage of the price differential.
He welcomed buying of Gazprom shares by Russian investors, and said it was not right that non-residents should benefit in this way.
"The fear is that somebody (a non-resident) will buy all of the stock up cheaply, which would just not be correct," Vyakhirev said.
He said Gazprom had told investors not to try to buy shares in this way, and that in some cases potential investors had backed away.
Earlier this year Cayman Islands-registered Regent Gaz Investment fund backed down from a planned $200-million fund backed by domestic Gazprom shares bought by a Regent subsidiary in Russia.
Gazprom threatened to act against Regent, which stopped its efforts.
Vyakhirev said the company fully intended to maintain limits of foreign participation in the group.
"To open up shares fully to foreign investors is simply not right," Vyakhirev said.
"If we look a long way into the future...then we could do everything completely freely. But today that is not the case," he said.
